deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematical derivation on this page. It holds three kinds of material.

(1) A Latin draft, continuing the draft on the previous page, of Riemann's formal petition to the Göttingen Philosophical Faculty to be admitted to the doctorate.
- Heading: 'Ab amplissimo philosophorum ordine ... decano clarissimo', partly struck.
- A curriculum-vitae paragraph. On his parents' advice, and with his father not unwilling, he arrived at the start of the summer semester of 1846 (MDCCCXLVI). This was shortly after the Johanneum (Lüneburg) sent him with the certificate of maturity (Abitur) to the Georgia Augusta. He gave up theology to devote himself to mathematics.
- Signature: 'G. F. B. Riemann, [Breselenzensis, struck], stud. math.'
- The petition proper. He says he has devoted himself for five years ('per quinquennium', 1846-1851) to mathematical and physical studies. He asks the faculty to make him doctor of philosophy, despite knowledge 'quae sentio quam sit exigua'.
- As a specimen of worthiness he has written a dissertation 'quae in jaciendis fundamentis theoriae generalis functionum complexae quantitatis variabilis versatur'. This is the published title of his 1851 Inaugural-Dissertation, 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. He submits it to their judgement.
- Dated Göttingen, 'die XXVIII[?] mensis Octobris anni MDCCCLI'. The previous page's version is dated 1 October 1851.

(2) Fee and expense jottings for the promotion.
- 'Approbation[?] 11', 'Schreiber[?] 4'.
- 'Promotion 13 Ldr 18 ggl', apparently equated with 71 (a crossed-out 65 has been replaced by 71). This reads as a conversion of 13 Louis d'or plus 18 gute Groschen into roughly 71 Thaler; the exchange rate is not legible or certain.
- Left-margin figures 6½, 2, 2, 36, 1 continue the household accounts begun on the previous page.

(3) Lower half, written upside down in Kurrent and largely illegible. To judge from the next page (which begins 'Es fragt sich, wenn die Veränderliche ... von x und y stetig abhängend ...'), this is probably a German draft of the opening of the dissertation. That opening concerns the notion of a function of the complex variable z = x + yi and the requirement that dw/dz be independent of direction. This reading is plausible but cannot be verified from the image.
errors: The internal arithmetic of the fee notes (13 Ldr 18 ggl = 71) cannot be confirmed without knowing the Louis d'or/Thaler rate assumed. At 5 Thaler per Louis d'or the total would be about 65¾, which matches the struck-out 65. The 71 implies a higher rate (about 5.4 Thaler per Ldr).

results.what: Latin draft of the doctoral petition and vita for the Göttingen Philosophical Faculty, naming the dissertation on the foundations of a general theory of functions of a complex variable (October 1851)
Expense/fee accounting for the promotion (approval fee, copyist, 13 Ldr 18 ggl promotion fee)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an administrative and biographical draft (doctoral petition, vita, fee notes). Its facts (1846 matriculation, switch from theology, 1851 dissertation on complex function theory) are well documented in Riemann biographies, e.g. Dedekind's Lebenslauf. There is no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: The 'quinquennium' of study from summer semester 1846 (MDCCCXLVI) to 1851 (MDCCCLI) is five years, consistent with the dates on the page.
13 Louis d'or plus 18 gute Groschen at 5 Thaler per Ldr and 24 ggl per Thaler gives 65.75 Thaler, which matches the struck-out '65'. The corrected '71' implies a different exchange rate.

transcription_corrections: '[-Breselenzensis-][?]' is very likely the struck-out 'Breselenzensis' (of Breselenz, Riemann's birthplace). The previous page's '{+Breslenzins[?],+}' should read the same.
'semestri{+a+}[?] aestivo' should be 'semestri aestivo' (ablative); the 'a' interlinear is uncertain.
The heading's second line reads approximately '[quisque] decano clarissimo', mostly struck. The interlinear word may be 'quoque' rather than 'quisque'.
'Vobis {+viri+} [-maxime venerandi-]': in the image the insertion appears to be 'viri maxime venerandi', with part struck. The uncertain sequence 'et me ob meam harum' has 'et me' corrected.
'Approbation[?] — 11 ℔[?]' and 'Schreiber[?] — 4 ℔[?]': the unit sign is probably a Thaler/currency abbreviation, not a pound sign.
The upside-down Kurrent block is probably a German draft related to the opening of the dissertation (cf. next page). It is not merely illegible notes.
